newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks continue upward bounce at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks continue upward bounce at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks powered ahead on strong turnover at the close Thursday, extending the bounce sparked Tuesday by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony, dealers said.

"The market continued its rebound, cheered by the strong earnings of Banco Frances, which drove the price of that stock and a few others like (holding firm) Perez Companc and (steelmaker) Siderca to all-time highs," said Luis Corsiglia at brokers Corsiglia y Cia.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 1.8 percent to 836.12, stretching gains since Tuesday to 5.7 percent.
It had shed 1.4 percent Monday and 5.7 percent last week on the back of devaluation fears in Brazil.
"The Brazil scare seems to be over and the market is heading for record levels of 900," Corsiglia said.
Traders noted the international economic scenario was ideal to fuel the recovery of the bolsa, which peaked at a five-year high of 856 earlier this month.

"The Dow is pushing further into record territory and long bond yields are stable below 6.5 percent. What more could we ask for?," another dealer said. "What's more, the earnings season has got off to a good start with Banco Frances."

Morgan Stanley raised Banco Frances Thursday to outperform from underperform, saying it was likely to benefit from a benign U.S. interest rate outlook and strong Argentine economic growth. Banco de Bilbao Vizcaya in May bought a 71.8 percent stake in Banco Frances.
The bolsa's broad market index closed up 2.1 percent Thursday, with winners pounding losers 59 to 10 and 14 issues closing flat.
Floor volume rose to a hefty tally of 45.8 million pesos from 39.4 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover soared to 331.1 million pesos from 231.4 million Wednesday.

Best main-tier performers were carmaker Ciadea, which jumped 6.6 percent, Banco de Galicia and Banco Frances, which gained 5.0 percent and 4.3 percent, respectively, gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, up 4.3 percent, and oil company Astra, up 3.8 percent.
Worst MerVal losers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa and steelmaker Acindar, which fell 1.7 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively.
